text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

Thank you for getting in touch. I can help your family talk this through. I cannot give legal advice or move money, but I can keep track of everyone's concerns and help you look for a plan.

Here is the list I am keeping. I will resend it whenever it changes.

1. C will not agree to A buying the house at a family discount.
2. C has asked that B receive some money from the estate.

Please tell me what you would want a fair outcome to look like, and I will add it.
A fair outcome means I get my fair financial share, and B receives some money too. I’m not agreeing to subsidize A’s purchase; no amounts or shares are settled yet.

I am helping your family work through the house and the will after your father's death. Your sister C asked me to assist.

Here is the list of concerns I am keeping so far.

1. C will not agree to A buying the house at a family discount.
2. C wants her fair financial share, and she wants B to receive some money too. No amounts or shares are settled yet.

I would like to hear your side directly. What are you and your husband proposing for the house, and what matters most to you? I will add your concerns to the list and share the updated version with the family.
My husband and I want to buy the house at a family discount, but I know we need C’s agreement. Financial independence matters most to me. I only know C hasn’t agreed yet—not that she won’t.

I am helping your family work through the house and the will after your father's death. Your sister C asked me to assist.

I’d be grateful if the estate could leave me with some money to start a dance studio. I’m not sure what should happen with the house yet, and I don’t think any shares or amounts are settled.

2. C wants her fair financial share, and she wants B to receive some money too. No amounts or shares are settled yet.
3. A and her husband want to buy the house at a family discount. A knows she needs C's agreement, and financial independence matters most to her.
4. B would like the estate to leave her some money to start a dance studio. She is undecided about the house, and she agrees no shares or amounts are settled.

May I ask A what discount she has in mind, and whether she would be open to a price closer to market value if it means an agreement C can accept?
We haven’t settled on a discount or price, and I’m not ready to name one. I’d consider discussing a price C could accept, but I can’t promise what we’d agree to.

I’m not sure yet. I haven’t worked out a figure, and I don’t think it’s settled what the estate can provide.

Since nobody is naming figures yet, a neutral next step would help: an independent valuation of the house. It would give all three of you the same starting number, and it does not commit anyone to anything. Would you support that, and would you be willing to name the share you consider fair?
Yes, I support an independent valuation. I’m not ready to name a share until we have the valuation and the relevant estate details.

C supports an independent valuation of the house, and she will talk about shares once we have it and the estate details. C is not ready to name a share yet either.
